description: PulteGroup is one of the largest homebuilders in the U.S., having constructed over 800,000 homes since 1950. The company operates in more than 45 markets across 24 states through its portfolio of brands, including Centex, Pulte Homes, Del Webb, DiVosta Homes, American West, and John Wieland Homes and Neighborhoods.

Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
After weathering a difficult year in a nearly frozen housing market, PulteGroup fell seven places from its 2023 ranking. Yet it remains the third largest homebuilder in the U.S., with operations in more than 45 U.S. markets. PulteGroup aims to create affordable housing opportunities; provides mortgage-free homes to wounded veterans through its Built to Honor program; organizes food drives with local pantries; and launches fundraising initiatives for organizations employees care about. 
 

The PulteGroup Foundation launched Dollars for Doers in 2022: For every hour an employee volunteers, the foundation contributes the equivalent of up to $25 per hour, for up to 40 hours annually per employee. 
 

To bolster the success of its homebuilding operations team, which constitutes 75% of its workforce, PulteGroup offers mentorship and formal training programs, such as its Certified Field Trainer initiative to support trainees for up to six months.

To bolster the success of its homebuilding operations team, which constitutes 75% of its workforce, PulteGroup offers mentorship and formal training programs, such as its Certified Field Trainer initiative to support trainees for up to six months.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
One of the largest homebuilders in the U.S. aims to continually improve the employee experience. As a result, nine out of 10 employees want to work at PulteGroup for “a long time.”

  • The diversity board’s outreach committee has enhanced PulteGroup’s recruitment, hiring, and onboarding efforts with a focus on identifying a large pool of diverse job candidates and building recruitment relationships with HBCUs.

  • New hires are assigned an onboarding experience partner, responsible for ensuring new team members feel connected to the company.

  • PulteGroup’s affordable housing committee is piloting a new program, Hope to Home, that will subsidize a percentage of the homes the company builds, offering them to first-time buyers in underserved groups.

  • The company has a one-stop learning management system that provides employees with training, workshops, and developmental tools.

  • PulteGroup’s new health and wellness program goes beyond physical and emotional health coverage to include financial and social wellness.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: America’s third-largest homebuilder has a laser focus on diversity, equity, and inclusion. PulteGroup created internal committees to work on recruiting and training a diverse talent pool of employees and to sponsor cultural awareness programming with live, interactive webinars that spotlight the achievements of a diverse range of individuals. Externally, in keeping with the company’s values, PulteGroup is working to create homeowning opportunities for lower-income families and minorities through affordable housing and down payment assistance initiatives. Part of the company’s emphasis on inclusion includes a flexible workweek. Once fully implemented, employees will work in the office two days per week and remotely for the other three.

I have several close friends working for other builders and they cannot say the same. I’m a proud Pulte employee!”

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: The homebuilder was hit hard by the pandemic, which forced it to make painful staff reductions in the form of furloughs and layoffs. In response, PulteGroup CEO Ryan Marshall, his direct reports, and the entire board of directors took pay cuts, raising $400,000 for a relief fund aiding those who lost their jobs. In the end, the company was able to bring back 100% of furloughed employees within 60 days, and actively set about rehiring those who were laid off. Marshall has also made a commitment to improving PulteGroup’s diversity practices, forming an internal diversity and inclusion board meant to hold the organization accountable to its goals.
